algorithm: Losslessly decode the native reader's tagged Erlang terms; distinguish atom, binary, tuple, list and map values.
Mask comment and literal text while retaining physical rows and character positions. Check native comment coverage and literal start positions. Interpolation code remains visible.

Use native do/end and fn closing coordinates to own explicit headers and written closers. Use native arrow coordinates for each pattern/guard clause header. A binding/call prefix belongs to its first executable header.
Use native multi-expression blocks and match operators to expand packed independent statements and chained assignments. Do not expand destructuring variable count.
Keep keyword-only do: definitions/conditionals as expressions. Preserve literal/data wrapping, counting physical nonblank/noncomment rows outside explicit executable owners.
Suppress only proved enclosing argument/data closing punctuation after executable closers. Never discard following real code.

Resolve scalar composition after fn and value-producing explicit if/unless/case/cond/for/with/try/receive controls using enclosing native AST expression ancestry: sequence siblings, clause bodies and do/else bodies supply exact expression bounds. A scalar continuation on the closer's physical row adds no independent unit; a continuation on another physical row retains that row's baseline unit. A packed next expression keeps its own unit. Module and named-function declarations do not receive this continuation rule.

The lexical composition review case in canonical.py:415-421 is resolved only for a continuation proved to belong to the same native expression. The same ownership rule applies to anonymous-function values and explicit control values. Continuations containing matches, independent expression sequences or another executable owner remain review cases. All expression bounds are emitted for inspection.

Emit diagnostics and a null normalized_loc for missing/mismatched/overlapping owner metadata, unsupported explicit macros, unowned executable tokens, assignment within data, or independent work inside interpolation.

Replay saved original and formatted AST/source artifacts, compare original native grammar fixtures with rule expectations, and sum each plan's authored application bundle only when every source has an unambiguous candidate count.

output_interpretation.normalized_loc: Unqualified candidate count; null when any ownership diagnostic exists.
output_interpretation.candidate_normalized_loc: Diagnostic aid only; may be present even when the canonical candidate is rejected.
output_interpretation.candidate_formatted_loc: Physical nonblank/noncomment rows of the native formatter artifact, kept separate from canonical LOC.
output_interpretation.candidate_canonical_loc: Sum of all original-source candidate counts in one authored bundle; null when any source is ambiguous.
output_interpretation.canonical_loc: Always null at replay profile level; this tool cannot admit a chart count.
output_interpretation.native_reader_terminal_verified: Always false; process completion/provenance belongs to the existing source-reader controller and its independently reviewed terminal receipt.
output_interpretation.qualification: Actual native parser replay, successful native fixture assertions, original-source owner review, formatter semantic evidence, and verified reader completion are still required. Synthetic AST tests do not replace these observations.

source_only_validation.source_review: Independent source review closed for the covered grammar and synthetic fixtures.

continuation_owner_correction.observed_case: Native spectralnorm AST places for/end inside the same pipeline expression as the following List.to_tuple call. Its same-row tail previously gained an extra unit while equivalent fn scalar tails did not.
continuation_owner_correction.scope: Reuse the existing bounded scalar-continuation accounting for fn and value-producing explicit controls; preserve body/header/closer owners, separate physical continuation rows, independent next statements and complex-tail rejection.
